digest.component_or_area: Jira DC harness CI — capability mapping and environment contract
propositions: On-demand CI workflow must map Jira DC image capability by booting the digest-pinned amd64 image and interrogating it with structured checklists, producing committed data (raw request/response evidence) not live discovery, to replace the 35-minute trial-and-error loop that repeated three times for a single question about issue type availability.

The mapping job must be manually dispatched only (workflow_dispatch, never push/PR/schedule), produce a reviewed artifact with traceable evidence, and never mutate the harness or re-run discovery at test time — it is an authoring tool for environment contracts, not a test harness component.

The job must validate all four rebar hardcoded vocabularies (issue types, statuses+workflows, priorities, link types) against the instance, detecting presence, absence, misspelling, unreachable states, and (for link types) inverted direction through end-to-end creation experiments, not name-only checks.

The job must measure five field length limits (summary 254, label 255, comment 32767, description 32767, ADF 32000) live at limit-1/limit/limit+1 with read-back verification to detect accept-and-truncate, and read jira.text.field.character.limit from instance config rather than assume 32767.

The environment contract answers must be committed as data in docs/jira-dc-capability-map.md and consumed by harness setup assertion _assert_project_capabilities, which derives nothing at test time, so answers cannot drift from declared state.

The map's staleness must be checkable by deriving the image digest from the Dockerfile FROM line (not a second literal), committing it as asserted data alongside the capability findings, and gating against re-pin so a changed image is detected before stale answers are acted upon.
